O.content: The title reads "Additional Top Stores: Ad Spend vs Sales".
Five blue points are visibly labeled Store 6, Store 7, Store 8, Store 9, and Store 10.
The horizontal axis is labeled "Advertising Spend ($ thousands)" and the vertical axis is labeled "Sales ($ thousands)".
No profitability, margin, ROI, or full-store-population inscription is visible.

B.text: If approval of a broader ad-spend increase requires evidence covering the relevant store population and profitability or ROI, then a chart limited to a subset of stores and showing only spend and sales should be routed for full-data analysis rather than approved.
B.conditions: Assumes the title defines the displayed population as additional top stores, and that the stated approval standard requires full-population and profitability/ROI evidence; neither requirement is printed as a policy rule on the chart.

O.content: From Store 6 through Store 10, the labeled blue points are successively farther right and higher on the page.
The horizontal axis is labeled "Advertising Spend ($ thousands)" and the vertical axis is labeled "Sales ($ thousands)".

B.text: If the horizontal axis encodes advertising spend and the vertical axis encodes sales on comparable scales, then points that progress upward and rightward across the displayed stores indicate a positive observed spend-sales association; this supports broader approval only if association in this subset is accepted as sufficient evidence of benefit.
B.conditions: Assumes axis labels bind to point coordinates and comparable observations; association does not establish causation, profitability, or generalization beyond the displayed stores.
